title: Dead Battery, Live Audience
麥克風沒電，台下有四百人
paras: More than four hundred {{attendee|attendees}} had filled the ballroom for the opening session of a retail technology {{forum|forum}}, where store owners and software companies compare notes. Megan Shaw stepped on stage to give the keynote, clipped on her {{microphone|microphone}}, and said good morning. Nobody heard a word.
超過四百位與會者坐滿了宴會廳，參加一場零售科技論壇的開幕場次。在這場論壇上，店家和軟體公司會互相交流心得。梅根．蕭走上台準備做主題演講，夾上麥克風，說了聲早安。沒有人聽到半個字。

"Check the {{battery|battery}}!" a voice called from the third row. A technician ran up, swapped in a fresh one, and Megan started again. Then the {{projector|projector}} flickered and went black. "{{whoever|Whoever}} set up this room left that cable loose," someone muttered. Megan laughed. "Okay. We'll do this the old-fashioned way."
「檢查一下電池！」第三排有人喊。一位技術人員跑上台換了新電池，梅根重新開講。接著投影機閃了幾下就黑掉了。「不管是誰布置這個會場的，都沒把那條線固定好。」有人小聲嘀咕。梅根笑了。「好吧，那我們就用老方法。」

She walked to the edge of the stage and began to talk about her own shop, and how a handwritten sign had once brought in more sales than a whole advertising campaign. Halfway through, a man near the aisle {{interrupt|interrupted}} her. "Sorry to cut in, but is that story true?" "Every word," Megan said. "I still have the sign." The room laughed, and for the first time that morning it felt like a conversation.
她走到舞台邊緣，開始談自己的店，說有一次一張手寫的告示牌，帶來的買氣比整個廣告活動還多。講到一半，靠走道的一位男士打斷了她：「抱歉打岔，這個故事是真的嗎？」「句句屬實，」梅根說，「那塊告示牌我還留著。」全場笑了，那個早上第一次有了像是在聊天的感覺。

By the time the technician got the projector working again, Megan no longer needed it. Later, at the welcome {{reception|reception}}, people lined up to shake her hand. "I'll post my notes online tonight," she told them. "That way they're {{accessible|accessible}} to everyone, even people who never saw a slide."
等技術人員把投影機修好時，梅根已經用不到它了。之後的歡迎茶會上，大家排隊跟她握手。「我今晚會把講稿放上網，」她對他們說，「這樣每個人都看得到，連沒看到投影片的人也一樣。」
